props.title: Live music for your anniversary party.
props.lede: The song they danced to at their wedding starts again, years later, and everyone who was there the first time is watching. An anniversary party is a dinner built around that song: a jazz duo or a singer with a guitar under the toasts, the song learned for the night, and a band on the floor afterward if the party dances.

items.q: Can we hire a band for an anniversary party?
items.a: Yes. Most anniversaries are a seated dinner with a toast, so a jazz duo or a singer with a guitar plays the dinner, and a trio or a quartet plays the anniversary that ends on a dance floor. It's one contract with one personal contact for the music, booked through Signet Artists in Denver.

items.q: Can the band play the couple's first-dance song?
items.a: Yes. The song from the wedding is learned for the night if it isn't already in the book, and one learned song comes with every booking. Tell us the title with the date, and whether it should be played or sung.

items.q: How does a surprise anniversary party work with a musician?
items.a: The musician is set up early and playing quietly, so the place looks like it simply has live music that night, and the couple's song starts on a cue you agree beforehand: a nod from the host or a text from a friend at the next table.

items.q: How loud is the music at dinner?
items.a: About as loud as the conversation at the table, so the toasts are easy to hear and nobody leans in to talk. The duo stops for each toast, and an announcement microphone is ready for whoever stands up. The musicians set the level to the space, so a restaurant's private dining space gets less than a backyard.

items.q: How much space does the band need at a dinner?
items.a: A guitarist or a singer with a guitar takes about 6 by 4 feet on one circuit, a duo 8 by 6 on one, a trio 12 by 8 on one and a quartet 14 by 10 on two, in the corner the table naturally faces. Setup runs 45 minutes for a solo and an hour for a duo or a trio. A certificate of insurance and a W-9 come with the quote if the venue asks.
